about.title: Pinole Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Pinole's mix of warehouses, retail centers along San Pablo Avenue, and delivery routes feeding I-80 means workplace injuries here often involve more than one company. A warehouse worker hurt by faulty equipment, a delivery driver struck on I-80 Eastbound while making a job stop, or a contractor injured on a site owned by someone other than their employer may have options beyond the workers' comp system alone. California generally requires injured workers to report a workplace incident to their employer within 30 days to preserve benefits, and retaliation for filing a claim is against the law. Separately, if a third party — a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer — contributed to the injury, a civil claim may be possible alongside workers' comp, though it carries its own two-year filing window. We help injured workers in Pinole explore which paths apply to your situation, at no cost unless there's a recovery.

items.title: We Help Untangle Comp vs. Third-Party Claims
items.desc: California workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party can still be held separately liable. We can review the facts and determine whether your Pinole injury opens the door to an additional claim.

items.title: We Understand the 30-Day Reporting Window
items.desc: California law generally requires reporting a workplace injury to the employer within 30 days to protect benefit eligibility. We make sure injured workers get prompt guidance so this deadline isn't missed.

items.title: No Cost Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered. That applies whether the case involves workers' comp, a third-party claim, or both.

items.question: I was hurt driving for work near the I-80/San Pablo Avenue interchange — is that just a workers' comp case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. If another driver, a vehicle defect, or a third party's negligence contributed to the crash, you may have a separate injury claim in addition to workers' comp. We can look at the specifics of your Pinole incident and explain which claims may apply.

items.question: What happens if my employer retaliates after I report an injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' comp claim is illegal in California. If you believe you've faced retaliation, we can advise you on your options separate from the underlying injury claim.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury or file a claim?
items.answer: California generally expects workplace injuries to be reported to the employer within 30 days to preserve workers' comp benefits. If a third party is involved, that separate civil claim typically carries a two-year deadline, so it's worth getting prompt guidance.
